Crypto Leverage Calculator

Margin, position size and leverage are one equation — set any two and the third follows, along with the distance to liquidation.

How it is calculated

leverage = position / margin   |   liq distance ≈ (1 − MMR) / leverage

Leverage is not a setting to max out — it is the ratio between the position you control and the collateral behind it. The higher it goes, the closer liquidation moves: at 10x the price only needs to travel roughly 10% against you; at 100x, about 1% — inside the random noise of a single candle on most coins.

Worked example

$100 margin holding a $1,000 position = 10x. With a 0.5% maintenance margin, liquidation sits roughly 9.95% below entry on a long. Every 1% move changes your margin by 10% — a normal 3% daily swing is a 30% equity swing at this size.

FAQ

What leverage do most professionals actually use?

Serious futures traders rarely run effective leverage above 3-5x on the whole account, even when an exchange offers 100x. High per-trade leverage is mainly a capital-efficiency tool: it lets you lock less margin for the same deliberately-sized position — not a way to multiply the bet.

Is liquidation the same as my stop-loss?

No. Liquidation is the exchange force-closing you when margin runs out — you lose the whole margin plus liquidation fees. A stop-loss is your own exit at a price you chose. If liquidation is doing the job of your stop, the position was oversized.

Why is my real liquidation price slightly different?

Exchanges compute liquidation from the maintenance-margin tier of your exact position size, plus fees, and for isolated vs cross margin differently. The distance formula here is the standard approximation for an isolated position and lands very close for typical sizes.
